{{Generations Sidebar}}'''Generation Z''' (or Gen Z for short), colloquially known as '''Zoomers''',<ref name="Wordswatching23">{{cite web |date=October 2021 |title=Words We're Watching: 'Zoomer' |url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/words-at-play/words-were-watching-zoomer-gen-z |access-date=October 25, 2021 |website=Merriam-Webster}}</ref><ref name="zoomer Dictionary.com">{{cite web|title=zoomer|url=https://www.dictionary.com/e/slang/zoomer/|access-date=14 June 2020|website=Dictionary.com|date=January 16, 2020 }}</ref> is the demographic [[Cohort (statistics)|cohort]] succeeding [[Millennials]] and preceding [[Generation Alpha]].<ref name="Williams-2015a">{{Cite news|last=Williams|first=Alex|date=September 19, 2015|title=Meet Alpha: The Next 'Next Generation'|work=The New York Times|department=Fashion|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/19/fashion/meet-alpha-the-next-next-generation.html|access-date=September 7, 2019}}</ref>

Members of [[Generation Z]], were born between the mid-to-late 1990s and the early 2010s, with the generation typically being defined as those born from 1997 to 2012. In other words, the first wave came of age during the latter half of the second decade of the twenty-first century,<ref name="Lexico-2019">{{Cite web|url=https://www.lexico.com/en/definition/generation_z|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817140603/https://www.lexico.com/en/definition/generation_z|archive-date=August 17, 2019|title=Generation Z|website=Lexico|publisher=Oxford English Dictionary|access-date=August 17, 2019}}</ref> a time of significant demographic change due to declining birthrates, population aging, and immigration.<ref name="Pew-2018a" /> Americans who grew up in the 2000s and 2010s saw gains in IQ points,<ref name="Flynn-2018">{{Cite journal|last1=Flynn|first1=James R.|last2=Shayer|first2=Michael|date=January–February 2018|title=IQ decline and Piaget: Does the rot start at the top?|journal=Intelligence|volume=66|pages=112–121|doi=10.1016/j.intell.2017.11.010|author-link=James R. Flynn (academic)}}</ref> but loss in creativity.<ref name="Kim-2011">{{Cite journal|last=Kim|first=Kyung Hee|date=2011|title=The Creativity Crisis: The Decrease in Creative Thinking Scores on the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking|journal=Creativity Research Journal|volume=23|issue=4|pages=285–95|doi=10.1080/10400419.2011.627805|s2cid=10855765}}</ref> They also reach puberty earlier than previous generations.<ref name=":45" /><ref name="Weir-20162" /><ref name=":2" />

On the whole, they are financially cautious,<ref name="Miller-2019c">{{Cite news |last=Miller |first=Ryan |date=April 12, 2019 |title=Forget the dream wedding. Gen Z-ers are planning to own homes before they're 30, survey finds |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/personalfinance/real-estate/2019/04/11/generation-z-already-saving-buy-home-bank-america-survey-says/3438279002/ |access-date=June 12, 2019 |work=USA Today}}</ref><ref name="Solmon-2019b">{{Cite news |last=Solmon |first=Paul |date=May 16, 2019 |title=What Gen Z college grads are looking for in a career |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/what-gen-z-college-grads-are-looking-for-in-a-career |access-date=May 17, 2019 |work=PBS Newshour}}</ref> and are increasingly interested in alternatives to attending institutions of higher education,<ref name="Solman-2019">{{Cite news |last=Solman |first=Paul |date=March 28, 2019 |title=Anxious about debt, Generation Z makes college choice a financial one |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/anxious-about-debt-generation-z-makes-college-choice-a-financial-one |access-date=May 12, 2019 |work=PBS Newshour}}</ref><ref name="Industry Week-2019">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=July 24, 2019 |title=Can Gen Z Save Manufacturing from the 'Silver Tsunami'? |url=https://www.industryweek.com/talent/can-gen-z-save-manufacturing-silver-tsunami |access-date=July 27, 2019 |work=Industry Week}}</ref> with young men being primarily responsible for the trend.<ref name="Belkin-2021">{{Cite news |last=Belkin |first=Douglas |date=September 6, 2021 |title=A Generation of American Men Give Up on College: 'I Just Feel Lost' |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/college-university-fall-higher-education-men-women-enrollment-admissions-back-to-school-11630948233 |access-date=September 11, 2021 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref><ref name="Thompson-2021" />

They became familiar with the Internet and portable digital devices at a young age (as "[[digital native]]s"),<ref name="Lexico-2019" /> but are not necessarily [[Digital literacy|digitally literate]],<ref name="Strauss-2019" /> and tend to struggle in a digital work place.<ref name=":282">{{Cite news |last=Hunter |first=Tatum |date=March 8, 2023 |title=What's a scanner? Gen Z is discovering workplace tech. |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2023/03/08/office-tech-young-old/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230310171035/https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2023/03/08/office-tech-young-old/ |archive-date=March 10, 2023 |access-date=May 13, 2023 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref><ref name=":27">{{Cite news |last=Wells |first=Georgia |date=August 24, 2024 |title=Gen Z-ers Are Computer Whizzes. Just Don't Ask Them to Type. |url=https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/gen-z-typing-computers-keyboards-c83d15f0 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240825050403/https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/gen-z-typing-computers-keyboards-c83d15f0 |archive-date=August 25, 2024 |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref> The majority use at least one social-media platform,<ref name=":21" /> leading to concerns that spending so much time on social media can distort their view of the world,<ref name="Pincott-2022">{{Cite journal |last=Pincott |first=Jena |date=June 2022 |title=Chasing Chaos |journal=Psychology Today |pages=42–5}}</ref> hamper their social development,<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Haidt |first=Jonathan |date=May 2022 |title=Why the Past 10 Years of American Life Have Been Uniquely Stupid |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2022/05/social-media-democracy-trust-babel/629369/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240513131917/https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2022/05/social-media-democracy-trust-babel/629369/ |archive-date=May 13, 2024 |access-date=June 11, 2024 |work=The Atlantic}}</ref> harm their mental health,<ref name="Goldfield-2023" /><ref name="Prinstein-2023" /><ref name="Smyth-2023" /><ref name="Schwartz-2023">{{Cite news |last=Schwartz |first=Casey |date=April 20, 2023 |title=Jean Twenge is ready to make you defend your generation again |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/books/2023/04/20/generations-jean-twenge-boomers-gen-z-millennials/ |access-date=April 21, 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230420182419/https://www.washingtonpost.com/books/2023/04/20/generations-jean-twenge-boomers-gen-z-millennials/ |archive-date=April 20, 2023}}</ref><ref name="Reed-2023">{{Cite news |last=Reed |first=Tina |date=March 27, 2023 |title=Pushback grows over mental health impacts of social media |work=Axios |url=https://www.axios.com/2023/03/27/pushback-grows-social-media |access-date=April 21, 2023}}</ref> expose them to inappropriate materials,<ref name="Pickhardt-2023" /><ref name=":31">{{Cite news |last=Gibson |first=Caitlin |date=September 25, 2024 |title=The dark revelations of a new documentary about teens and social media |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/2024/09/25/lauren-greenfield-teens-documentary/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240925121122/https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/2024/09/25/lauren-greenfield-teens-documentary/ |archive-date=September 25, 2024 |access-date=October 22, 2024 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> and cause them to become addicted.<ref name=":21" /><ref name=":20">{{Cite news |last1=Sy |first1=Stephanie |last2=Dubnow |first2=Shoshana |date=December 26, 2023 |title=States suing Meta accuse company of manipulating its apps to make children addicted |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/states-suing-meta-accuse-company-of-manipulating-its-apps-to-make-children-addicted |access-date=January 23, 2023 |work=PBS Newshour}}</ref> Although they trust traditional news media more than what they see online,<ref name="Business Wire-2019">{{Cite news |last= |first= |date=June 20, 2019 |title=New Barnes & Noble Education Report Finds Gen Z Will Have Strong Influence on 2020 Presidential Election |work=Business Wire (via AP) |url=https://apnews.com/Business%20Wire/15122922e4fc4e91a314b8cdc383ff61 |access-date=June 22, 2019}}</ref> they tend to be more skeptical of the news than their parents.<ref name="Reuters-2019" />

While a majority of young Americans of the late 2010s held politically left-leaning views,<ref name="Pew-2019b" /> Generation Z has been shifting towards the right since 2020.<ref name=":42" /><ref name=":44" /> But most members of Generation Z are more interested in [[Careerism|advancing their careers]] than pursuing idealistic political causes.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Moreover, there is a significant sex gap,<ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Moon |first1=Phoebe W. |last2=Kim |first2=Hannah June |date=March 31, 2024 |title=The Growing Gender Divide: Changing Perceptions of Gender Equality among the Youth in the United States |url=https://iasr.or.kr/_common/do.php?a=full&b=&bidx=3615&aidx=40108 |journal=International Area Studies Review |volume=27 |issue=1 |pages=1–20 |doi=10.69473/iasr.2024.27.1.1|url-access=subscription }}</ref> with implications for families, politics, and society at large.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Why young men and women are drifting apart |url=https://www.economist.com/international/2024/03/13/why-the-growing-gulf-between-young-men-and-women |access-date=2025-01-31 |newspaper=The Economist |issn=0013-0613}}</ref> As voters, members Generation Z do not align themselves closely with either major political parties;<ref name=":7">{{Cite news |last1=Yang |first1=John |last2=Baldwin |first2=Lorna |last3=Mufson |first3=Claire |date=September 8, 2024 |title=New book explores how Gen Z's politics differ from previous generations |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/new-book-explores-how-gen-zs-politics-differ-from-previous-generations |access-date=September 21, 2024 |work=PBS News Hour}}</ref> their top issue is the economy.<ref name=":9" /> As consumers, Generation Z's actual purchases do not reflect their environmental ideals.<ref name="The Economist-2023a" /><ref name="The Economist-2023b" /> Members of Generation Z, especially women, are also less likely to be religious than older cohorts.<ref name="Jones-2022">{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Jeffrey M. |date=June 17, 2022 |title=Belief in God in U.S. Dips to 81%, a New Low |url=https://news.gallup.com/poll/393737/belief-god-dips-new-low.aspx |access-date=December 27, 2022 |website=Gallup}}</ref><ref name=":15" />

Although American youth culture has become highly fragmented by the start of the early twenty-first century, a product of growing individualism,<ref name="Twenge-2023">{{Cite book |last=Twenge |first=Jean |title=Generations: The Real Differences Between Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X and Silents—and What The Mean for America's Future |publisher=Atria Books |year=2023 |isbn=978-1-9821-8161-1 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter 1: The How and Why of Generations}}</ref> nostalgia is a major feature of youth culture in the 2010s and 2020s.<ref name="Jan-2022" /><ref name=":26">{{Cite news |last=Mirabelli |first=Gabriella |date=November 15, 2019 |title=Why Nostalgia Appeals to Younger Audiences (Guest Column) |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/why-nostalgia-appeals-younger-audiences-guest-column-1255137/ |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=Hollywood Reporter}}</ref>

== Nomenclature and date range ==
{{Main|Generation Z#Etymology and nomenclature|Generation Z#Date and age range}}

{{Quote box
| quote = While there is no scientific process for deciding when a name has stuck, the momentum is clearly behind Gen Z.|
| author = Michael Dimmock, [[Pew Research Center]] (2019)<ref name="Dimmock">{{cite web|last=Dimmock|first=Michael|date=January 17, 2019|title=Defining generations: Where Millennials end and post-Millennials begin|url=http://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2018/03/01/defining-generations-where-millennials-end-and-post-millennials-begin/|access-date=December 21, 2019|publisher=Pew Research Center}}</ref>
| align = left
| width = 25%
| quoted = 1
}}The name ''Generation Z'' is a reference to the fact that it follows Generation Y (Millennials).<ref>{{cite book|last=Shapiro|first=Jordan|title=The New Childhood: Raising Kids to Thrive in a Connected World|publisher=Little, Brown|year=2018}}</ref> Other proposed names for the generation include ''iGeneration'',<ref name="Horovitz2">{{cite news|last=Horovitz|first=Bruce|date=4 May 2012|title=After Gen X, Millennials, what should next generation be?|newspaper=USA Today|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/gen-millennials-generation/story?id=16275187|access-date=24 November 2012}}</ref> ''Homeland Generation'',<ref name="ForbesHomeland2">{{cite magazine|last1=Howe|first1=Neil|date=27 October 2014|title=Introducing the Homeland Generation (Part 1 of 2)|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/neilhowe/2014/10/27/introducing-the-homeland-generation-part-1-of-2/#7420cde74fdc|magazine=Forbes|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> ''Net Gen'',<ref name="Horovitz2" /> ''Digital Natives'',<ref name="Horovitz2" /> ''Neo-Digital Natives'',<ref name="Thomas2">{{Cite book|last=Thomas|first=Michael|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=z8Kahia4IQEC|title=Deconstructing Digital Natives: Young People, Technology, and the New Literacies|date=19 April 2011|publisher=Taylor & Francis|isbn=978-1-136-73900-2|language=en}}</ref><ref name="Japanese Youth and Mobile Media2">{{cite news|last1=Takahashi|first1=Toshie T|title=Japanese Youth and Mobile Media|publisher=Rikkyo University|url=https://www.academia.edu/350038|access-date=10 May 2016}}</ref> ''Pluralist Generation'',<ref name="Horovitz2" /> ''Centennials'',<ref name="Centennials 22">{{Cite web|title=Meet Generation Z|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/pictures/meet-generation-z/6/|access-date=January 15, 2021|work=CBS News|date=September 22, 2015 |quote=Generation Z is also hugely synonymous with technology because Centennials grew up in the era of smartphones. In fact, most of today's youth can't even remember a time before social media.}}</ref> and ''Post-Millennials''.<ref name="Pew-2016">{{cite web|date=25 April 2016|title=Millennials overtake Baby Boomers as America's largest generation|url=http://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2016/04/25/millennials-overtake-baby-boomers/|access-date=18 September 2016|website=Pew Research Center|publisher=Pew Research}}</ref> The term ''Internet Generation'' reflect that the generation is the first to have been born after the mass-adoption of the [[Internet]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Generations in Canada|url=https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/census-recensement/2011/as-sa/98-311-x/98-311-x2011003_2-eng.cfm|website=www12.statcan.gc.ca}}</ref> In the U.S., the term ''Generation Z'' is overwhelmingly the most popular. ''Zoomer'' is an [[Slang|informal term]] often used in an ironic, humorous, or ridiculing tone. It combines the term ''boomer,'' referring to baby boomers, with the "Z" from ''Generation Z''. Prior to this, ''Zoomer'' was used in the 2000s to describe particularly active baby boomers.<ref name="Wordswatching23" /> ''Zoomer'' in its current incarnation skyrocketed in popularity in 2018, when it was used in an [[Internet meme]] ridiculing Gen Z adolescents.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Tiffany|first=Kaitlyn|date=February 3, 2020|title=The Misogynistic Joke That Became a Goth-Meme Fairy Tale|url=https://www.theatlantic.com/technology/archive/2020/02/doomer-girl-meme-4chan-tumblr-wojak-history/605764/|website=The Atlantic}}</ref> Merriam-Webster's records suggest the use of the term ''zoomer'' in the sense of Generation Z dates back at least as far as 2016. It was added to the dictionary in 2021.<ref name="Wordswatching23" />

In January 2019, [[Pew Research Center]] defined "Post-Millennials" as people born from 1997 onward, choosing this date for "different formative experiences" for the purposes of demographic analysis.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dimock |first=Michael |title=Defining generations: Where Millennials end and Generation Z begins |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2019/01/17/where-millennials-end-and-generation-z-begins/ |access-date=2023-08-28 |website=Pew Research Center |date=January 17, 2019 |language=en-US}}</ref> Common generational experiences include technological developments and socioeconomic trends, including the widespread availability of wireless internet access and high-bandwidth cellular service, and key world events, such as growing up in a world after the [[September 11 attacks|September 11th terrorist attacks]].<ref>{{cite web |title=What We Know About Gen Z So Far |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/social-trends/2020/05/14/on-the-cusp-of-adulthood-and-facing-an-uncertain-future-what-we-know-about-gen-z-so-far-2/ |website=Pew Research Center's Social & Demographic Trends Project |date=14 May 2020}}</ref> During a 2019 analysis, Pew stated that they have yet to set an endpoint to Generation Z, but did use the year 2012 to complete their analysis.<ref name="Pew Research Center-2018b">{{cite web|date=March 1, 2018|title=Defining generations: Where Millennials end and post-Millennials begin|url=http://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2018/03/01/defining-generations-where-millennials-end-and-post-millennials-begin/|publisher=Pew Research Center}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Burclaff |first1=Natalie |title=Research Guides: Doing Consumer Research: A Resource Guide: Generations |url=https://guides.loc.gov/consumer-research/market-segments/generations |website=guides.loc.gov |access-date=21 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Meola |first1=Andrew |title=Generation Z News: Latest characteristics, research, and facts |url=https://www.insiderintelligence.com/insights/generation-z-facts/ |website=Insider Intelligence |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Tyson |first1=Alec |last2=Kennedy |first2=Brian |last3=Funk |first3=Cary |title=Gen Z, Millennials Stand Out for Climate Change Activism, Social Media Engagement With Issue |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/science/2021/05/26/gen-z-millennials-stand-out-for-climate-change-activism-social-media-engagement-with-issue/ |website=Pew Research Center Science & Society |date=26 May 2021}}</ref> Jason Dorsey of the Center for Generational Kinetics also cites Pew Research's 1997–2012 range to define Gen Z in a 2025 article.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dorsey |first=Jason |date=2025-06-17 |title=Jason Dorsey Featured in Reader’s Digest on Generational Identity |url=https://jasondorsey.com/blog/featured-in-readers-digest-on-generational-identity/ |access-date=2026-03-06 |website=Jason Dorsey |language=en-GB}}</ref> In a 2022 article, [[United States census|U.S. Census]] economists Neil Bennett and Briana Sullivan described Generation Z as those born 1997 to 2013.<ref>{{cite web |publisher=United States Census Bureau |title=2019 Data Show Baby Boomers Nearly 9 Times Wealthier Than Millennials |url=https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2022/08/wealth-inequality-by-household-type.html |access-date=18 February 2023 |website=Census.gov}}</ref> Psychologists Jean Twenge and [[Jonathan Haidt]] argue that even though the concept of a social generation remains debated, there is evidence for significant differences between the different demographic cohorts.<ref name="Schwartz-2023"/> Those born between (on [[Cusper|the cusp]] of) the [[Millennial]] generation and [[Generation Z]] are commonly known as [[Zillennials]].<ref name="Zennials">{{cite book |author1=Hannah L. Ubl |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pZuqDgAAQBAJ |title=Managing Millennials For Dummies |author2=Lisa X. Walden |author3=Debra Arbit |date=24 April 2017 |publisher=John Wiley & Sons |isbn=978-1-119-31022-8 |page=266 |chapter=Chapter 13: Making Adjustments for Ages and Life Stages}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The American Generations: Names, Years, & Key Differences {{!}} Britannica |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/Experience-the-American-Generations-Which-Generation-Are-You-2226598 |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=www.britannica.com |language=en}}</ref> Those born (on the cusp of) [[Generation Z]] and [[Generation Alpha]] are commonly known as [[Zalphas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zalpha micro-generation |first=McCrindle |title=What Is a Zalpha |url=https://mccrindle.com.au/article/what-is-a-zalpha/ |website=McCrindle |date=November 21, 2023 }}</ref>

==Arts and culture==

=== General trends ===
[[File:USNS Comfort passing by Statue of Liberty, March 30, 2020.png|thumb|Hospital ship [[USNS Comfort|USNS ''Comfort'']] entering [[New York Harbor]] in March 2020 in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, a major global crisis that took place during the formative years of Generation Z<ref name="Twenge-2023b">{{Cite book |last=Twenge |first=Jean |author-link=Jean Twenge |title=Generations: The Real Differences Between Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X and Silents—and What They Mean for America's Future |publisher=Atria Books |year=2023 |isbn=978-1-9821-8161-1 |location=New York |chapter=Event Interlude: The COVID-19 Pandemic}}</ref>]]
Given their birth years, members of Generation Z have no memory of the time before the terrorist attacks on [[September 11 attacks|September 11, 2001]], and the subsequent [[war on terror]].<ref name="Woodruff-2021">{{Cite news |last=Woodruff |first=Judy |date=September 8, 2021 |title=How 9/11 weighs heavy on the generation born after the 2001 attacks |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/how-9-11-weighs-heavy-on-the-generation-born-after-the-2001-attacks |access-date=September 11, 2021 |work=PBS Newshour}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Column: High-maintenance Generation Z heads to work |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/news/opinion/forum/story/2012-06-27/generation-z-work-millenials-social-media-graduates/55845098/1 |access-date=17 December 2015 |website=USATODAY.COM}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Palmer |first=Alun |date=1 August 2014 |title=Are you X, Y, Z, Boomer or Silent Generation – what does it mean for you? |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/you-x-y-z-boomer-3950868 |website=[[Daily Mirror]]}}</ref> Yet even twenty years after the attacks had taken place, concerns over national security as well as personal safety remain.<ref name="Woodruff-2021" /> But most members of Generation Z were in their formative years during the [[2008 financial crisis]].<ref name="turner2">{{cite journal |last1=Turner |first1=Anthony |year=2015 |title=Generation Z: Technology And Social Interest |journal=Journal of Individual Psychology |volume=71 |issue=2 |pages=103–113 |doi=10.1353/jip.2015.0021 |s2cid=146564218}}</ref> A 2013 survey found that 47% of Generation Z in the United States (considered here to be those between the ages of 14 and 23) were concerned about [[student debt]], while 36% were worried about being able to afford a higher education at all.<ref name="Forbes2013">{{cite web |author=Henderson, J Maureen |date=31 July 2013 |title=Move Over, Millennials: Why 20-Somethings Should Fear Teens |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/jmaureenhenderson/2013/07/31/move-over-millennials-why-twentysomethings-should-fear-teens/ |access-date=5 November 2015 |work=Forbes}}</ref> This generation is facing a growing income gap and a shrinking middle-class, which all have led to increasing stress levels in families.<ref name="turner2" /> According to [[Public Relations Society of America]], the [[Great Recession]] has taught Generation Z to be independent, and has led to an entrepreneurial desire, after seeing their parents and older siblings struggle in the workforce.<ref>{{cite web |last=Dupont |first=Stephen |date=10 December 2015 |title=Move Over Millennials, Here Comes Generation Z: Understanding the 'New Realists' Who Are Building the Future |url=https://www.prsa.org/Intelligence/Tactics/Articles/view/11057/1110/Move_Over_Millennials_Here_Comes_Generation_Z_Unde |website=Public Relations Tactics |publisher=Public Relations Society of America}}</ref> Psychologist Jean Twenge describes Generation Z as "uniquely pessimistic" compared to older cohorts.<ref name=":54">{{Cite news |last=Twenge |first=Jean |date=June 20, 2025 |title=The Myth of the Gen Z Red Wave |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2025/06/gen-z-red-wave/683212/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250622013622/https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2025/06/gen-z-red-wave/683212/ |archive-date=June 22, 2025 |access-date=June 22, 2025 |work=The Atlantic}}</ref>

The [[COVID-19 pandemic]] struck when the oldest members of Generation Z was just joining the workforce and the rest were still in school.<ref name="Twenge-2023b" /> For this reason, it split Generation Z into two small cohorts with drastically different lived experiences,<ref name=":28">{{Cite news |last=Janfaza |first=Rachel |date=March 19, 2025 |title=How covid tore Generation Z in two |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2025/03/19/covid-gen-z-generational-divide/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250319103913/https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2025/03/19/covid-gen-z-generational-divide/ |archive-date=March 19, 2025 |access-date=March 19, 2025 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref> and this gap has been widened by the rapid pace of [[technological change]], not just video-sharing platforms—especially TikTok—but also generative artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, notably [[ChatGPT]].<ref name=":28" /> Consequently, the two sub-groups of Generation Z not only have different worldviews in general but also different politics.<ref name=":22">{{Cite news |last=Janfaza |first=Rachel |date=April 26, 2025 |title=The New Partisan Divide Is Old Gen Z vs. Young Gen Z |url=https://www.politico.com/news/magazine/2025/04/26/two-gen-zs-young-conservative-polling-00307375 |access-date=May 3, 2025 |work=Politico Magazine}}</ref>

Growing up in such uncertain times, Generation Z has come to embrace nostalgia, longing for a purportedly simpler age, or things that remind them of their childhood,<ref name=":26" /> or even of eras before they were born.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Routledge |first=Clay |date=August 24, 2025 |title=What Is Gen Z So Nostalgic for? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/24/opinion/gen-z-technology-nostalgia.html |access-date=March 31, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> As a result, they adapt, hybridize, and modernize cultural artifacts in efforts to connect to the past, but without abandoning modern electronic devices, which enable them to experience the idealized past at will.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Faust |first=Ella |date=December 22, 2019 |title=How Gen Z Hears the Sirens of the Past |url=https://commonreader.wustl.edu/c/how-gen-z-hears-the-sirens-of-the-past/ |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=The Common Reader |publisher=Washington University, St. Louis}}</ref>

Jean Twenge describes Generation Z as "slow [[Life history theory|life-history strategists]]"—meaning they delay taking part in adult activities such as drinking alcohol, having sexual intercourse, or driving, as a consequence of their [[#Upbringing|upbringing]].<ref name="Twenge-2017">{{Cite news |last=Twenge |first=Jean |date=September 19, 2017 |title=Why today's teens aren't in any hurry to grow up |url=https://theconversation.com/why-todays-teens-arent-in-any-hurry-to-grow-up-83920 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |work=The Conversation}}</ref><ref name="Twenge-2023a">{{Cite book |last=Twenge |first=Jean |title=Generations: The Real Differences Between Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X, Boomers, and Silents—and What The Mean for America's Future |publisher=Atria Books |year=2023 |isbn=978-1-9821-8161-1 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter 6: Generation Z}}</ref> Interest in sports has also declined noticeably compared to older generations.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tracy |first=Jeff |date=March 4, 2021 |title=Generation Alpha kids carry on trend of declining interest in sports |url=https://www.axios.com/2021/03/04/sports-interest-kids-generation-elpha |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=Axios}}</ref>

A 2014 study ''Generation Z Goes to College'' found that Generation Z students self-identify as being loyal, compassionate, thoughtful, open-minded, responsible, and determined.<ref name="Seemiller-2016">{{Cite book |last=Seemiller |first=Corey |title=Generation Z Goes to College |publisher=Jossey-Bass |year=2016 |isbn=978-1-119-14345-1}}</ref> How they see their Generation Z peers is quite different from their own self-identity. They view their peers as competitive, spontaneous, adventuresome, and curious—all characteristics that they do not see readily in themselves.<ref name="Seemiller-2016" /> Like all other cohorts born after the Second World War, Generation Z is culturally individualistic and values social equality. But unlike older living generations of their time, members of Generation Z are much more likely to identify as gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, or otherwise [[Gender nonconformity|non-conforming]].<ref name="Twenge-2023a" />

Museums from across the United States significantly expanded their programs aimed at children, including K-12 students, during the 2000s and 2010s, according to the [[American Alliance of Museums]] and the [[Institute of Museum and Library Services]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 24, 2018 |title=Museum Facts & Data |url=https://www.aam-us.org/programs/about-museums/museum-facts-data/ |access-date=June 20, 2019 |website=American Alliance of Museums}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2019 |title=Public Libraries in the United States - Fiscal Year 2016 |url=https://www.imls.gov/sites/default/files/publications/documents/public-libraries-united-states-survey-fiscal-year-2016.pdf |access-date=July 5, 2019 |website=Institute of Museum and Library Services}}</ref>

=== News media ===
According to the [[Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism]], among Americans in their late teens and early 20s, the most common sources of news were social media (especially Facebook and YouTube).<ref name="Reuters-2019" /> Even so, they turn towards well-known news outlets to learn more about current events that interest them.<ref name="Reuters-2019" /> A 2019 survey by Barnes and Nobles Education found that ''The New York Times'', ''[[The Washington Post]]'', ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', CNN, and the ''[[USA Today]]'' are deemed the most trustworthy news sources by Generation Z. They also found that Generation Z consider traditional print media to be the most trustworthy while words of mouth and what they see on social media to be the least trustworthy.<ref name="Business Wire-2019" /> Nevertheless, while Generation Z understands the importance of traditional news agencies, they tend to be less loyal than their parents. Young Americans are concerned about the perceived bias, lack of context, negativity, and [[sensationalism]] in the news media. American youths today want news stories that are not only fun and meaningful but also accurate and fair.<ref name="Reuters-2019" /> A 2016 poll by Gallup found a decline in trust in the news media across all age groups since (at least) the 1990s, and people aged 18 to 49 are less likely than those 50 years of age or older to trust the media.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Swift |first=Art |date=September 14, 2016 |title=Americans' Trust in Mass Media Sinks to New Low |url=https://news.gallup.com/poll/195542/americans-trust-mass-media-sinks-new-low.aspx |access-date=July 2, 2019 |newspaper=Gallup.com}}</ref>

While visual story-telling has proven to be popular, 58% of Generation Z still prefer text to videos. This number goes up for people who are older.<ref name="Reuters-2019">{{Cite web|url=https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2019-06/DNR_2019_FINAL_0.pdf|title=Digital News Report 2019|website=Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, Oxford University|pages=55–59|access-date=June 12, 2019}}</ref> When asked what they would choose if they could have only one subscription, only 7% picked the news while 37% chose a video service and 15% selected music.<ref name="Cellan-Jones-2019">{{Cite news |last=Cellan-Jones |first=Rory |date=June 12, 2019 |title=Who will pay for trusted news? |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-48595593 |access-date=July 11, 2019 |work=BBC}}</ref>

=== Entertainment ===
The most popular forms of entertainment among Generation Z are playing video games, listening to music, surfing the Internet, and using social media networks.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Faughnder |first=Ryan |date=April 18, 2021 |title=What entertainment does Gen Z prefer? The answer isn't good for Hollywood |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2021-04-18/what-entertainment-does-gen-z-prefer-the-answer-isnt-good-for-hollywood |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220105080217/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2021-04-18/what-entertainment-does-gen-z-prefer-the-answer-isnt-good-for-hollywood |archive-date=January 5, 2022 |access-date=January 25, 2022 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=April 18, 2021 |title=Gen Z Ranks Watching TV, Movies as Fifth Among Top 5 Entertainment Activities |url=https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/gen-z-survey-deloitte-tv-movies-ranking-1234954207/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241013171805/https://variety.com/2021/digital/news/gen-z-survey-deloitte-tv-movies-ranking-1234954207/ |archive-date=October 13, 2024 |access-date=October 13, 2024 |work=Variety}}</ref> According to Asha Choksi, vice president of global research and insights for the educational publisher Pearson, about one in every three members of Generation Z spends at least four hours per day watching videos online.<ref name="Mirabella-2019">{{Cite news |last=Mirabella |first=Lorraine |date=May 3, 2019 |title=Get ready for Gen Z, employers. First hint: They're not millennials. |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2019/05/03/get-ready-for-gen-z-employers-first-hint-theyre-not-millennials/ |access-date=May 12, 2019 |work=Baltimore Sun}}</ref> Data from the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]] show that while people aged 15 to 24 spent more time playing video games in 2018, the time spent on computers and televisions remained virtually unchanged.<ref name="Ingraham-2019">{{Cite news |last=Ingraham |first=Christopher |date=June 21, 2019 |title=Screen time is rising, reading is falling, and it's not young people's fault |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2019/06/21/screen-time-is-rising-reading-is-falling-its-not-young-peoples-fault/ |access-date=June 27, 2019 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref>

In its 2018 Gen Z Music Consumption & Spending Report, digital media company Sweety High found that Generation Z was listening to more diverse music genres than generations past, whose music preferences solidified by early adolescence. [[Spotify]] was the most popular source of music for Generation Z (61%), followed by terrestrial radio ranked second (55%), while [[YouTube]] was the preferred platform for music discovery (75%).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/brittanyhodak/2018/03/06/new-study-spotlights-gen-zs-unique-music-consumption-habits/#9c217042d09b|title=New Study Spotlights Gen Z's Unique Music Consumption Habits|last1=Hodak|first1=Brittany|date=March 6, 2018|work=Forbes|access-date=June 13, 2019|publisher=}}</ref> [[TikTok]] is another major platform for music discovery and for Generation Z to connect with their favorite musicians.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Peoples |first=Glenn |date=September 21, 2020 |title=New Data Reveals Music's Importance to TikTok's Gen Z Audience |url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/new-data-reveals-music-importance-tiktok-gen-z-audience/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210908180049/https://www.billboard.com/articles/business/9453156/new-data-reveals-music-importance-tiktok-gen-z-audience/ |archive-date=September 8, 2021 |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=Bill Board}}</ref> Research on popular music from the 1950s to the 2010s has shown that this genre has become louder, while the chords, melodies, and types of sounds used have becoming increasingly homogenized.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wickham |first=Chris |date=July 26, 2012 |title=Pop music too loud and all sounds the same: official |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-science-music/pop-music-too-loud-and-all-sounds-the-same-official-idUSBRE86P0R820120726 |access-date=October 27, 2019 |work=Reuters}}</ref> At the same time, lyrics of the most popular songs have becoming less joyful, sadder, and angrier.<ref name=":10">{{Cite news |last=Lawrence Technological University |date=January 24, 2019 |title=Popular music lyrics become angrier and sadder over time |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2019/01/190124124737.htm |access-date=September 19, 2021 |work=Science Daily}}</ref> Such shifts have occurred due to changing consumer tastes.<ref name=":10" /> In particular, the melancholic lyrics of Billie Eilish and [[Olivia Rodrigo]] resonate with their generation.<ref name=":110">{{Cite news |last=Ryan |first=Patrick |date=January 27, 2020 |title=Who is Billie Eilish? Everything to know about the teen who won big at the 2020 Grammys |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/music/2020/01/27/billie-eilish-teen-pop-star-winner-grammy-awards-2020/4586132002/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521042357/https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/music/2020/01/27/billie-eilish-teen-pop-star-winner-grammy-awards-2020/4586132002/ |archive-date=May 21, 2021 |access-date=May 21, 2021 |work=USA Today |department=Music}}</ref><ref name=":122">{{Cite news |last=John |first=Sarah |date=May 22, 2021 |title=New Olivia Rodrigo album 'Sour' stakes her claim to being the voice of Gen Z: Raw and real |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/think/opinion/new-olivia-rodrigo-album-sour-stakes-her-claim-being-voice-ncna1268211 |access-date=May 22, 2021 |work=NBC News |department=Culture & Lifestyle}}</ref><ref name="Twenge-2023a" /> A 2019 poll by Ypulse found that for teenagers (13 to 18), the top musicians were [[Billie Eilish]] and [[Ariana Grande]] whereas among young adults (19 to 26), the most liked were [[Taylor Swift]] and Ariana Grande.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 8, 2019 |title=The 17 Musicians Gen Z & Millennials Say Represent Their Generations |url=https://www.ypulse.com/article/2019/10/08/the-17-musicians-gen-z-millennials-say-represent-their-generations/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20191101175747/https://www.ypulse.com/article/2019/10/08/the-17-musicians-gen-z-millennials-say-represent-their-generations/ |archive-date=November 1, 2019 |access-date=September 8, 2021 |work=Ypulse}}</ref>

Chinese music video app [[Musical.ly]] was highly popular among American teens.<ref name="Lee-2018">{{Cite book|title=AI Superpowers - China, Silicon Valley, and the New World Order|last=Lee|first=Kai-Fu|publisher=Houghton Mifflin Harcourt|year=2018|isbn=978-1-328-54639-5|location=United States of America|pages=108–109|chapter=Chapter 4: The Four Waves of AI}}</ref> In 2018, Musical.ly was shut down and its users were transferred to [[TikTok]].<ref name="Dave-2018">{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bytedance-musically/chinas-bytedance-scrubs-musical-ly-brand-in-favor-of-tiktok-idUSKBN1KN0BW|title=China's Bytedance scrubs Musical.ly brand in favor of TikTok|last=Dave|first=Paresh|date=August 2, 2018|work=Reuters|access-date=June 13, 2019}}</ref> By the early 2020s, TikTok has become one of the most popular social networks among teenagers and young adults in the United States.<ref name=":11">{{Cite news |last=McKinnon |first=John D. |date=March 13, 2023 |title=Biden's TikTok Dilemma: A Ban Could Hurt Democrats More Than Republicans |url=https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/bidens-tiktok-dilemma-a-ban-could-hurt-democrats-more-than-republicans-a74bcf2a |archive-url=https://archive.today/V1Qye |archive-date=March 13, 2023 |access-date=March 13, 2023 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref><ref name="Barinka-2023" />

==== Film and television ====
[[Cartoon Network]], the [[Disney Channel]], and [[Nickelodeon]] were once staples of children's entertainment among Millennials and Generation Z.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://variety.com/2007/scene/markets-festivals/high-school-musical-2-aces-test-1117970479/|work=Variety|first1=Rick|last1=Kissell|first2=Michael|last2=Schneider|title=''High School Musical 2'' aces test|date=August 18, 2007|access-date=2012-05-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209232746/http://www.variety.com/article/VR1117970479?refCatId=14|archive-date=2012-02-09|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2010/01/19/nickelodeon-scores-record-breaking-night-with-brand-new-icarly-and-big-time-rush-debut/39381/|title=Nickelodeon Scores Record-Breaking Night with Brand-New ''iCarly'' and ''Big Time Rush'' Debut - Ratings|last=Gorman|first=Bill|date=January 19, 2010|access-date=August 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103220807/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2010/01/19/nickelodeon-scores-record-breaking-night-with-brand-new-icarly-and-big-time-rush-debut/39381/|archive-date=November 3, 2012|publisher=Zap2it|website=TV By the Numbers}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Stevens |first=Matt |last2=Jacobs |first2=Julia |date=June 30, 2021 |title=Dan Schneider Once Reigned Over Children’s TV. What Happened? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/30/arts/dan-schneider-nickelodeon.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211117124633/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/30/arts/dan-schneider-nickelodeon.html |archive-date=November 17, 2021 |access-date=April 15, 2026 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> But viewership began to drop in the early 2010s.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/viacom-nielsen-investigating-inexplicable-nickelodeon-260149|title=Viacom, Nielsen Investigating 'Inexplicable' Nickelodeon Ratings Drop|last=Szalai|first=Georg|magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=November 10, 2011}}</ref> Nielsen figures for 2020 revealed that the viewership of children's cable [[Broadcast programming|linear television]] channels continued their steady decline despite the COVID-19 pandemic, which forced many parents and their children to stay at home, while streaming services saw healthy growth.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Low |first=Elaine |date=April 9, 2020 |title=Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network and other kids cable channels see viewership declines as streaming grows |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/coronavirus/ct-ent-cartoon-network-nickelodeon-see-viewership-declines-20200409-sa5z5zzrlzchzpxx34ejv77fe4-story.html |access-date=December 19, 2020 |work=Chicago Tribune}}</ref> Among members of Generation Z who regularly watch movies, demand for physical media ([[DVD]]s and [[Blu-ray]]s), both for sale and for rent, has been climbing in the 2020s.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Davies |first=Cerys |date=February 23, 2026 |title=DVDs are the new vinyl records: Why Gen Z is embracing physical media |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2026-02-23/why-gen-z-wants-to-buy-rent-dvds-blu-rays-in-age-of-streaming |access-date=May 14, 2026 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

Animations, including those made in Japan (known as [[anime]]), are in high demand among Generation Z.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cobb |first=Kayla |date=July 27, 2024 |title=Crunchyroll Is Thriving Thanks to Gen Z and Appointment Anime Viewing, COO Says |url=https://www.thewrap.com/crunchyroll-gita-rebbapragada-coo-interview/ |access-date=June 2, 2025 |work=The Wrap}}</ref><ref name=":49">{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2024 |title=Gen Z's TV Favorites: Which Shows Are Winning Over Young Viewers? |url=https://www.parrotanalytics.com/insights/gen-z-tv-favorite-shows-which-shows-are-winning-over-young-viewers/ |access-date=June 2, 2025 |website=Parrot Analytics}}</ref> By the mid-2020s, the most popular television series among Generation Z include ''[[My Hero Academia#Anime adaptation|My Hero Academia]]'' (2016–present), ''[[Steven Universe]]'' (2013–2019), ''[[Invincible (TV series)|Invincible]]'' (2021–present), ''[[Euphoria (American TV series)|Euphoria]]'' (2019–2026), ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' (2008–2020), and ''[[Loki (TV series)|Loki]]'' (2021–2023).<ref name=":49" /> Generations Z and Alpha also enjoy comfort television shows popular with older cohorts or ended before they were born, such as ''[[Friends]]'' (1994–2004) and ''[[Gilmore Girls]]'' (2000–2007; [[Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life|2016]]),<ref>{{Cite news |last=Battaglio |first=Stephen |date=December 23, 2025 |title=Why Gen Z and Gen Alpha are feasting on TV comfort food |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-12-23/why-gen-z-gen-alpha-are-feasting-on-tv-comfort-food |access-date=May 14, 2026 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref> as well as shows featuring characters roughly their age, like ''[[Young Sheldon]]'' (2017–2024) and ''[[Stranger Things]]'' (2016–2025), and long-running television drama, like ''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'' (2005–present).<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 17, 2023 |title=Gen Z and Millennials' Top 10 Favorite TV Shows Right Now |url=https://www.ypulse.com/article/2023/04/17/gen-z-and-millennials-top-10-favorite-tv-shows-right-now/ |access-date=June 29, 2023 |work=YPulse}}</ref> The [[Netflix]] science-fiction horror series ''Stranger Things'' became a popular TV series to Generation Z by using and evoking [[1980s nostalgia#Generation Z|nostalgia for the 1980s]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Orazi |first1=Davide Christian |last2=Laer |first2=Tom van |date=July 10, 2022 |title=It's not nostalgia. Stranger Things is fuelling a pseudo-nostalgia of the 1980s |url=http://theconversation.com/its-not-nostalgia-stranger-things-is-fuelling-a-pseudo-nostalgia-of-the-1980s-186389 |access-date=2022-08-23 |website=The Conversation |language=en}}</ref> A slight majority of Generation Z would like to see fewer instances of romance and sex in the movies and television programs they watch, and more of friendships, [[platonic love]], and other types of relationships,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Veltman |first=Chloe |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Looking for 'nomance': Study finds teens want less sex in their TV and movies |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/10/25/1208435267/sex-teens-tv-movies |access-date=October 21, 2024 |work=National Public Radio}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=May 1, 2024 |title=Is there more or less sex on screen? |url=https://www.economist.com/culture/2024/05/01/is-there-more-or-less-sex-on-screen |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250108031742/https://www.economist.com/culture/2024/05/01/is-there-more-or-less-sex-on-screen |archive-date=January 8, 2025 |access-date=June 9, 2025 |newspaper=The Economist}}</ref> including [[Cross-sex friendship|opposite-sex friendships]] that do not evolve into romantic or sexual relationships.<ref name=":51">{{Cite news |last=Horton |first=Adrian |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Almost half of gen Z viewers want less sex on screen, study finds |url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2023/oct/25/gen-z-less-sex-tv-movie-trend |access-date=June 9, 2025 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> Pluralities of this cohort also want to see more [[Aromanticism|aromantic]] or [[Asexuality|asexual]] characters.<ref name=":52">{{Cite news |last=Thompson |first=Jaden |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Gen Z Teens Want Less Sex on Screen, According to New UCLA Study |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/sex-on-screen-ucla-study-gen-z-teens-young-adults-1235768046/ |access-date=June 9, 2025 |work=Variety}}</ref> Even so, certain television series such as ''[[The Sex Lives of College Girls]]'' (2021–2025) and movies like ''[[Poor Things (film)|Poor Things]]'' (2023) have proven to be popular among younger audiences.<ref name=":34">{{Cite news |last=Barnes |first=Brook |date=October 24, 2024 |title=Teens to Hollywood: Enough Sex, Already |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/24/business/teens-movies-tv-sex.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241024160602/https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/24/business/teens-movies-tv-sex.html |archive-date=October 24, 2024 |access-date=October 28, 2024 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> A slight majority of Generation Z prefers films and movies with original plots to adaptations, franchises, and remakes.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hibberd |first=James |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Gen Z Wants Less Sex in Movies, TV: Study |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/gen-z-study-sex-movies-tv-1235627979/ |access-date=June 9, 2025 |work=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> In particular, they would like more contents that are authentic<ref name=":52" /> and that reflect their own lives.<ref name=":51" />

As members of Generation Z re-watch their favorite childhood films, some have become [[Cult film|cult classics]] for their cohorts, including ''[[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (film)|Charlie and the Chocolate Factory]]'' (2005),<ref>{{cite news |last=Sevverlz |first=Mayoorhan |date=April 26, 2022 |title=Why It's Important to Have Faith in ''Wonka'' |url=https://www.cbr.com/why-wonka-prequel-will-work/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220615111811/https://www.cbr.com/why-wonka-prequel-will-work/ |archive-date=June 15, 2022 |access-date=June 5, 2022 |work=[[Comic Book Resources]]}}</ref> ''[[Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith]]'' (2005),<ref>{{cite news |last=Sinclair Chappell |first=Caitlin |date=January 9, 2020 |title=Star Wars: Gen Z Has Turned Revenge of the Sith Into a Cult Classic |url=https://www.cbr.com/star-wars-gen-z-turned-revenge-of-the-sith-into-cult-classic/ |access-date=June 23, 2025 |work=[[Comic Book Resources]]}}</ref> and ''[[Aquamarine (film)|Aquamarine]]'' (2006).<ref>{{cite web |last=Bjornson |first=Greta |date=16 October 2020 |title=Is 'Aquamarine' on Disney+? |url=https://decider.com/2020/10/16/is-aquamarine-on-disney-plus/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210419123453/https://decider.com/2020/10/16/is-aquamarine-on-disney-plus/ |archive-date=19 April 2021 |access-date=22 January 2022 |website=[[Decider.com]]}}</ref> By the mid-2020s, Generation Z has become a key demographic group for movie theaters.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |last2=Lang |first2=Brent |date=July 15, 2026 |title=The Box Office Bounces Back: Gen Z, Surprise Hits and More Have Hollywood Banking on a $10 Billion Year |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/movie-theaters-rebound-box-office-obsession-project-hail-mary-1236810214/ |access-date=August 28, 2026 |work=Variety}}</ref> As they grow older, members of Generation Z still broadly prefer [[Motion Picture Association film rating system#Ratings|family-friendly]] movies,<ref>{{Cite news |last=McClintock |first=Pamela |last2=Ford |first2=Lily |date=March 11, 2026 |title=Can Gen Z Save Hollywood? |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/gen-z-movie-theaters-1236526243/ |access-date=May 13, 2026 |work=Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> such as the Disney film ''[[Lilo & Stitch (2025 film)|Lilo & Stitch]]'' (2025),<ref>{{Cite news |last=Galuppo |first=Mia |date=May 27, 2025 |title=''Lilo & Stitch'' and the Power of Zillennial Nostalgia at the Movie Theater |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-features/lilo-and-stitch-and-the-power-of-zillennial-nostalgia-1236231230/ |access-date=May 31, 2025 |work=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> and the summer blockbuster ''[[Spider-Man: Brand New Day]]'' (2026).<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 11, 2026 |title=Gen Z has rediscovered the joy of going to the movies |url=https://www.economist.com/culture/2026/08/11/gen-z-has-rediscovered-the-j |access-date=August 28, 2026 |work=The Economist}}</ref> The animated series ''[[Bluey (TV series)|Bluey]]'' (2018–present), despite being made for preschool children, has captured the imagination of many Millennials and members of Generation Z. Not only does it fuel their nostalgia and portrays family life optimistically, but also helps them recover from childhood [[Psychological trauma|emotional wounds]].<ref name=":210">{{Cite magazine |last=Tait |first=Amelia |date=January 23, 2023 |title=The Internet Is Breeding Hordes of Adult ''Bluey'' Fans |url=https://www.wired.com/story/bluey-internet-fandom/ |access-date=May 8, 2025 |magazine=Wired}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Balanzategui |first1=Jessica |last2=Baker |first2=Djoymi |date=May 1, 2024 |title=Why are adults without kids hooked on ''Bluey''? And should we still be calling it a 'kids' show'? |url=https://theconversation.com/why-are-adults-without-kids-hooked-on-bluey-and-should-we-still-be-calling-it-a-kids-show-228610 |access-date=May 5, 2024 |work=The Conversation}}</ref>

==== Reading ====
[[File:Booktok section, Barnes & Noble, The Grove, Hollywood, Los Angeles, California, USA.jpg|thumb|The BookTok section at a [[Barnes & Noble]] store in Los Angeles (2022). BookTok has led to a surge in volitional reading among Generation Z.<ref name=":50" />]] A longitudinal analysis from 1976 to 2016 concluded that "compared with previous generations, teens in the 2010s spent more time online and less time with traditional media, such as books, magazines and television. Time on digital media has displaced time once spent enjoying a book or watching TV." Between 2006 and 2016, usage of digital media, including social networking websites, increased among teenagers while the number of teenagers who read books in their spare time dropped.<ref name="Sliwa-2018">{{Cite news |last=Sliwa |first=Jim |date=August 20, 2018 |title=Teens Today Spend More Time on Digital Media, Less Time Reading |url=https://www.apa.org/news/press/releases/2018/08/teenagers-read-book |access-date=November 8, 2020 |work=American Psychological Association}}</ref><ref name="Twenge-2018">{{Cite journal |last1=Twenge |first1=Jean |last2=Martin |first2=Gabrielle |last3=Spitzberg |first3=Brian |date=2018 |title=Trends in U.S. Adolescents' Media Use, 1976-2016: The Rise of Digital Media, the Decline of TV, and the (Near) Demise of Print |journal=Psychology of Popular Media Culture |volume=8 |issue=4 |pages=329–345 |doi=10.1037/ppm0000203 |s2cid=158283705}}</ref> 

At school, teachers assign much shorter reading assignments than in the past, and they are less likely to require that students read full-length books.<ref name=":8">{{Cite news |last=Lurye |first=Sharon |date=September 17, 2024 |title=Not-so-great expectations: Students are reading fewer books in English class |url=https://apnews.com/article/books-reading-high-school-english-class-c8d9f39773268a6e8c79cb0b3c78d3c1 |access-date=September 21, 2024 |work=Associated Press}}</ref> But among teenagers who read for pleasure, [[dystopian fiction]], such as ''[[The Hunger Games]]'' and ''[[Divergent (book series)|Divergent]]'', has proven to be popular.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Nadworny |first=Elissa |date=December 18, 2017 |title=Why Teens Find The End Of The World So Appealing |url=https://www.npr.org/sections/ed/2017/12/18/536007249/why-teens-find-the-end-of-the-world-so-appealing |access-date=September 19, 2021 |work=NPR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Tinneny |first=Anna |date=August 16, 2018 |title=Generation Z Grew Up Reading Dystopias, Now We're Fighting To Stop One {{!}} Opinion |url=https://www.newsweek.com/2018/09/28/generation-z-grew-reading-dystopias-now-were-fighting-stop-one-opinion-1072305.html |access-date=September 27, 2022 |work=Newsweek}}</ref> In addition, the surge in reading during the 2000s coincided with the release of the ''[[Harry Potter]]'' and ''[[Twilight (novel series)|Twilight]]'' novels.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twenge |first=Jean |date=March 5, 2024 |title=Are books dead? Why Gen Z doesn't read |url=https://www.generationtechblog.com/p/are-books-dead-why-gen-z-doesnt-read |access-date=September 21, 2024 |website=Generation Tech}}</ref> Millennial and Gen-Z readers mostly prefer [[print book]]s to electronic ones. They also tend to like comic books, manga, and graphic novels more than text-only versions of the same stories.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Berens |first1=Kathi |last2=Noorda |first2=Rachel |date=January 12, 2024 |title=Gen Z and millennials have an unlikely love affair with their local libraries |url=https://theconversation.com/gen-z-and-millennials-have-an-unlikely-love-affair-with-their-local-libraries-220632 |access-date=January 5, 2025 |website=The Conversation}}</ref> Many members of Generation Z have joined [[BookTok]], a community on TikTok where people share and discuss  the books they read.<ref name=":50">{{Cite news |last=Mathis |first=Joel |date=February 14, 2024 |title=Gen Z is bringing back reading |url=https://theweek.com/culture-life/books/gen-z-reading-book-club-booktok |access-date=May 23, 2025 |work=The Week}}</ref> So influential is this book club among Generation Z that it has boosted reading for pleasure among this cohort.<ref name=":82">{{Cite web |last=Hue |first=Angelina |date=September 18, 2021 |title=TikTok is turning decade-old books into bestsellers for the first time as it inspires a reading renaissance |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/tiktok-booktok-inspiring-reading-renaissance-old-books-bestsellers-2021-9 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918143709/https://www.businessinsider.com/tiktok-booktok-inspiring-reading-renaissance-old-books-bestsellers-2021-9 |archive-date=September 18, 2021 |access-date=June 6, 2025 |website=Business Insider |language=}}</ref><ref name=":022">{{Cite news |last1=Harris |first1=Elizabeth A. |date=March 20, 2021 |title=How Crying on TikTok Sells Books |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/20/books/booktok-tiktok-video.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240919165512/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/03/20/books/booktok-tiktok-video.html |archive-date=September 19, 2024 |access-date=June 5, 2025 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> Even members of Generation Z who do not consider themselves readers enjoy visiting public libraries for social events, classes, or a sense of community.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lora |first=Kelly |date=December 28, 2023 |title=What Gen Z Is Finding at the Library |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/newsletters/archive/2023/12/library-gen-z-readers/676963/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240908233644/https://www.theatlantic.com/newsletters/archive/2023/12/library-gen-z-readers/676963/ |archive-date=September 8, 2024 |access-date=May 23, 2025 |work=The Atlantic}}</ref>

== Demographics ==
{{See also|Aging of the United States}}
[[File:Ethnic_Composition_of_US_Cohorts.png|center|700x700px]]

A report by demographer William Frey suggests that as of 2019, 50.9% of Generation Z is white, 13.8% is black, 25.0% Hispanic, and 5.3% Asian.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Frey|first=William|date=June 24, 2019|title=Less than half of US children under 15 are white, census shows|url=https://www.brookings.edu/research/less-than-half-of-us-children-under-15-are-white-census-shows/|access-date=December 4, 2020|website=Brookings Institution}}</ref> 29% of Generation Z are children of immigrants or immigrants themselves, compared to 23% of Millennials when they were at the same age. As of 2019, 13.7% of the U.S. population is foreign-born, compared to 9.7% in 1997, when the first members of Generation Z had their birth cries.<ref name="Kight-2019b">{{Cite news|last=Kight|first=Stef W.|date=December 14, 2019|title=Immigration is shaping the youngest generation of voters|work=Axios|url=https://www.axios.com/immigration-gen-z-voters-2020-presidential-election-33ee50d5-2863-4ab3-b9e5-3444a2926e8b.html|access-date=December 24, 2019|archive-date=December 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191224214420/https://www.axios.com/immigration-gen-z-voters-2020-presidential-election-33ee50d5-2863-4ab3-b9e5-3444a2926e8b.html}}</ref> Indeed, according to the Pew Research Center, in spite of the diminished flow of immigrants to the United States following the Great Recession, Generation Z is the most ethnically diverse yet seen. 52% of this generation is white. 25% is Hispanic. 14% is black, and 4% is Asian.<ref name="Pew-2018a" /> Approximately 4% is multiracial,<ref name="Pew-2018a" /> and this number has risen rapidly between 2000 and 2010.<ref name="Williams-2015" /> More specifically, the number of Americans who identify as mixed white and black has grown by 134% and those of both white and Asian extraction by 87%.<ref name="Williams-2015" /> For comparison, 44% of Millennials, 40% of Generation X, and 28% of the Baby Boomers identify as non-white.<ref name="Desjardins-2019" /> Research by the demographer Bill Frey suggests that at the national level, Hispanics and Asians are the fastest-growing racial minority groups in the United States while the number of Caucasians under the age of 18 has been declining since 2000.<ref name="Hart-2019">{{Cite news|url=https://www.axios.com/americas-race-diversity-population-1d8b2664-860d-4c9f-84a6-416af8421601.html|title=America's sweeping tide of diversity|last=Hart|first=Kim|date=September 11, 2019|work=Axios|access-date=September 16, 2019|archive-date=September 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190917150508/https://www.axios.com/americas-race-diversity-population-1d8b2664-860d-4c9f-84a6-416af8421601.html}}</ref> Overall, the number of births to Caucasian women in the United States dropped 7% between 2000 and 2018. Among foreign-born Caucasian women, however, the number of births increased by 1% in the same period. Although the number of births to foreign-born Hispanic women fell from 58% in 2000 to 50% in 2018, the share of births due to U.S.-born Hispanic women increased from 20% in 2000 to 24% in 2018. The number of births to foreign-born Asian women rose from 19% in 2000 to 24% in 2018 while that due to U.S.-born Asian women went from 1% in 2000 to 2% in 2018. In all, between 2000 and 2017, more births were to foreign-born than U.S.-born women.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pewresearch.org/fact-tank/2019/08/08/hispanic-women-no-longer-account-for-the-majority-of-immigrant-births-in-the-u-s/|title=Hispanic women no longer account for the majority of immigrant births in the U.S.|last=Livingston|first=Gretchen|date=August 8, 2019|work=Pew Research Center|access-date=November 3, 2019}}</ref><gallery mode="packed" heights="300">
File:Ethnic Composition of Americans Under 15.png|Ethnic minorities under the age of 15 have seen significant growth since the 2000s.
File:US population pyramid (2018).jpg|Population pyramid of the United States in 2018
</gallery>Members of Generation Z are slightly less likely to be foreign-born than Millennials;<ref name="Pew-2018a" /> the fact that more American Latinos are born in the U.S. rather than abroad plays a role in making the first wave of Generation Z appear better educated than their predecessors. However, researchers note that this trend could be altered by changing immigration patterns and the younger members of Generation Z choosing alternate educational paths.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2018/11/15/668106376/generation-z-is-the-most-racially-and-ethnically-diverse-yet|title=Generation Z Is The Most Racially And Ethnically Diverse Yet|last=Wang|first=Hansi|date=November 15, 2018|work=NPR|access-date=August 6, 2019}}</ref><ref group="note">See the section on [[#Post-secondary|post-secondary education]].</ref> 29% of Generation Z are children of immigrants or immigrants themselves, compared to 23% of Millennials when they were at the same age. As of 2019, 13.7% of the U.S. population is foreign-born, compared to 9.7% in 1997, when the first members of Generation Z had their birth cries.<ref name="Kight-2019b"/> For this cohort, the number of people born in the United States reached a peak of 4.3 million in 2007.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Calfas |first1=Jennifer |last2=DeBarros |first2=Anthony |date=April 23, 2025 |title=U.S. Fertility Rate Remains Near Record Low |url=https://www.wsj.com/us-news/u-s-fertility-rate-remains-near-record-low-d6324668 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250423193418/https://www.wsj.com/us-news/u-s-fertility-rate-remains-near-record-low-d6324668 |archive-date=April 23, 2025 |access-date=May 31, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref>

Not only are Americans becoming more and more racially diverse, but racial minorities are also becoming more geographically dispersed than ever before, as new immigrants settle in places other than the large metropolitan areas historically populated by migrants, such as New York City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. A majority of Generation Z live in urban areas and are less inclined to change address than their predecessors.<ref name="Pew-2018a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pewsocialtrends.org/2018/11/15/early-benchmarks-show-post-millennials-on-track-to-be-most-diverse-best-educated-generation-yet/|title=Early Benchmarks Show 'Post-Millennials' on Track to Be Most Diverse, Best-Educated Generation Yet|date=November 15, 2018|website=Pew Research Center|access-date=May 11, 2019}}</ref> Similar to the Millennials, roughly two thirds of Generation Z come from households of married parents. By contrast, this living arrangement was essentially the norm for Generation X and the Baby Boomers, at 73% and 85%, respectively.<ref name="Pew-2018a" />

As a demographic cohort, Generation Z is smaller than the Baby Boomers or their children, the Millennials.<ref name="Kight-2019a">{{Cite news|last=Kight|first=Stef W.|date=December 14, 2019|title=Young people are outnumbered and outvoted by older generations|work=Axios|url=https://www.axios.com/2020-election-youth-vote-gen-z-895c7c4b-3ee2-4068-8b83-96178249d3f0.html|access-date=December 24, 2019|archive-date=December 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191224214437/https://www.axios.com/2020-election-youth-vote-gen-z-895c7c4b-3ee2-4068-8b83-96178249d3f0.html}}</ref> (See [[population pyramid]].) According to the [[United States Census Bureau|U.S. Census Bureau]], Generation Z makes up about one quarter of the U.S. population.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/kathryndill/2015/11/06/7-things-employers-should-know-about-the-gen-z-workforce/#71b200cfad7e|title=7 Things Employers Should Know About The Gen Z Workforce|last=Dill|first=Kathryn|date=November 6, 2015|website=Forbes|access-date=May 11, 2019}}</ref> This demographic change could have social, cultural, and political implications for the decades ahead.<ref name="Hart-2019" /> Generation Z are usually the children of [[Generation X]],<ref name="Williams-2015">{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/20/fashion/move-over-millennials-here-comes-generation-z.html|title=Move Over, Millennials, Here Comes Generation Z|last1=Williams|first1=Alex|date=18 September 2015|access-date=8 April 2016|work=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.acui.org/Publications/The_Bulletin/2014/2014-10/26390/|title=Gen Z: Unlike the Generation Before|last1=Beltramini|first1=Elizabeth|date=October 2014|access-date=8 April 2016|publisher=Associations of College Unions International|archive-date=April 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160424013827/https://www.acui.org/Publications/The_Bulletin/2014/2014-10/26390/}}</ref> and sometimes Millennials.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.aarp.org/home-family/friends-family/info-2016/technology-and-millennials-children-mq.html|title=The Scoop on Millennials' Offspring — Gen Z|last1=Quigley|first1=Mary|date=7 July 2016|access-date=9 July 2016|publisher=AARP}}</ref> Jason Dorsey, who works for the Center of Generational Kinetics, observed that Generation Z is not an extreme version of the Millennials but is rather different, and the differences can largely be attributed to parenting. Like parents from Generation X, members of Generation Z tend to be autonomous and pessimistic. They need validation less than the Millennials and typically become financially literate at an earlier age as many of their parents bore the full brunt of the Great Recession.<ref name="Boyle-2019">{{Cite news|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/money/markets/reality-bites-back-to-understand-gen-z-look-to-the-gen-x-parents/ar-AAF0Xaj|title=Reality bites back: To understand Gen Z, look to the Gen X parents|last1=Boyle|first1=Matthew|date=July 31, 2019|work=Bloomberg (via MSN)|access-date=August 4, 2019|last2=Townsend|first2=Matthew}}</ref>

== Economic trends and outlooks ==

=== Spending and savings habits ===

==== Consumer behavior ====
Modern technology has enabled Generation Z to take advantage of the on-demand economy, defined as "the economic activity created by technology companies that fulfill consumer demand via the immediate provisioning of goods and service."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.businessinsider.com/the-on-demand-economy-2014-7|title=The 'On-Demand Economy' Is Revolutionizing Consumer Behavior|last1=Mike|first1=Jaconi|website=Tech Insider|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> Generation Z tends to value utility and quality over brand name.<ref name="Forbes-2017">{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/differences-between-generation-z-and-millennials-money-2017-6|title=Research shows how Generation Z thinks differently from millennials when it comes to money|date=June 7, 2017|website=Forbes|access-date=May 12, 2019}}</ref> Authenticity is critical. Having been raised by Generation X and grown up in a recession, members of Generation Z are quick to verify claims. Being consistent users of the Internet and social media in particular, they frequently employ these tools to learn more about a certain product or service they are interested in. Product specifications, vendor ratings, and peer reviews are all important.<ref name="Pinnegar-2019" /> They tend to be skeptical and will shun firms whose [[Value-action gap|actions and values are contradictory]].<ref name="The Economist-2023a">{{Cite news |date=January 19, 2023 |title=How to sell to the young |newspaper=The Economist |url=https://www.economist.com/leaders/2023/01/19/how-to-sell-to-the-young |access-date=January 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230122104027/https://www.economist.com/leaders/2023/01/19/how-to-sell-to-the-young |archive-date=January 22, 2023}}</ref><ref name="The Economist-2023b">{{Cite news |date=January 16, 2023 |title=How the young spend their money |newspaper=The Economist |url=https://www.economist.com/business/2023/01/16/how-the-young-spend-their-money |access-date=January 29, 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230128084943/https://www.economist.com/business/2023/01/16/how-the-young-spend-their-money |archive-date=January 28, 2023}}</ref> There is a fair amount of interest in in-person shopping rather than over the Internet,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Silverman |first=Ellie |date=July 3, 2019 |title=Generation Z still prefers shopping in stores, study finds |url=https://www.inquirer.com/business/generation-z-brands-google-apple-itunes-snapchat-facebook-online-shopping-20190703.html |access-date=July 4, 2019 |work=Philadelphia Inquirer}}</ref> a potentially positive development for [[Brick and mortar|brick-and-mortar stores]].<ref name="Wu-2019">{{Cite news |last=Wu |first=Jasmine |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Gen Z shopping habits can fuel a brick-and-mortar resurgence, report says |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/09/17/gen-z-shopping-habits-can-fuel-a-brick-and-mortar-resurgence-report-says.html |access-date=September 23, 2019 |work=CNBC}}</ref> Products with comprehensible ingredients and simple packaging are preferred.<ref name="Wu-2019" /> In recognition of the tastes of large segments of Generation Z, the next cohort of young consumers, a number of brands, such as [[M&M's]], have moved their advertising and mascots away from the sexual appeal and towards a more anxious but casual style.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Heil |first=Emily |date=January 21, 2022 |title=M&M's candy mascots get a makeover, with less sex appeal and more Gen-Z anxiety |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/food/2022/01/21/mandms-rebrand-personalities/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240521014351/https://www.washingtonpost.com/food/2022/01/21/mandms-rebrand-personalities/ |archive-date=May 21, 2024 |access-date=October 11, 2024 |newspaper=The Washington Post}}</ref><ref name="Twenge-2023a" /> Generation Z's shopping habits are affected by social media networks and their impact on mental health.<ref name="Williams-2019">{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Robert |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Gen Z's worries about emotional health affect shopping habits, study says |url=https://www.marketingdive.com/news/gen-zs-worries-about-emotional-health-affect-shopping-habits-study-says/563055/ |access-date=September 23, 2019 |work=Marketing Dive}}</ref> Gen-Z consumers are less likely to [[Conspicuous consumption|pay a premium]] for what they want compared to their counterparts from emerging economies.<ref name="The Economist-2023b" /> While majorities might [[Virtue signalling|signal]] their support for certain ideals such as "environmental consciousness" to pollsters, actual purchases do not reflect their stated views, as can be seen from their high demand for cheap but not durable clothing ("[[fast fashion]]"), or preference for rapid delivery.<ref name="The Economist-2023a" /><ref name="The Economist-2023b" /> Overall, although more than half say they sought environmentally friendly products, only 38% are willing to pay extra for them.<ref name="Wu-2019" /> While majorities of older cohorts prefer American products, Generation Z is mixed on whether or not to buy goods made in China.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Koop |first=Avery |date=July 19, 2023 |title=Does "Made in America" Still Matter to Consumers? |work=Visual Capitalist |url=https://www.visualcapitalist.com/made-in-america-vs-made-in-china/ |access-date=July 31, 2023}}</ref>[[File:Hey Jude by The Beatles (Vinyl-1988).jpg|right|thumb|Young people are [[Vinyl revival|nostalgically preserving vinyl records]], among other items of the past.<ref name="Jensen-2019">{{Cite news |last=Jensen |first=Erin |date=November 18, 2019 |title=Hold your heads high, millennials and Gen Z! There are (at least) 6 things you haven't ruined |work=USA Today |department=Life |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/2019/11/18/millennials-gen-z-traditional-items-they-havent-killed/4180942002/ |access-date=November 28, 2019}}</ref>]]Nostalgia is a major theme of the behavior of consumers from Generation Z. For example, 2000s vintage electronics and fashion are back in vogue by the early 2020s.<ref name="YPulse-2020">{{Cite news |date=February 18, 2020 |title=Gen Z Is Bringing the 2000s Back…Here's How Brands Can Keep Up |work=YPulse |url=https://www.ypulse.com/article/2020/02/18/gen-z-is-bringing-the-2000s-back-heres-how-brands-can-keep-up/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last1=Rosenblatt|first1=Kalhan|last2=Wilson|first2=Lauren|date=July 25, 2021|title=Gen Z's 'nowstalgia' for Y2K fashion is leading to a thrifting explosion|work=NBC News|department=Pop Culture News|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/pop-culture/pop-culture-news/gen-z-s-nowstalgia-y2k-fashion-leading-thrifting-explosion-n1274720|access-date=September 19, 2021}}</ref> Youths who came of age during the 2010s and 2020s feel [[Nostalgia|nostalgic]] about "simpler" eras of history they have never experienced due to the uncertainties and stress of modern life, with student loan debts and the threat of terrorism being the top concerns.<ref name="Jan-2022">{{Cite news |last=Jan |first=Risi |date=September 27, 2022 |title=Why Do Younger Generations Feel Nostalgic for a Past They Never Experienced? |work=Newsweek |url=https://www.newsweek.com/why-do-younger-generations-feel-nostalgic-past-they-never-experienced-1746377 |access-date=December 29, 2022}}</ref><ref name=":26" /> Despite having the reputation for "killing" many things valued by older generations, Millennials and Generation Z are nostalgically preserving [[Instant camera|Polaroid cameras]], [[Phonograph record|vinyl records]], [[needlepoint]], and home gardening, to name just some.<ref name="Jensen-2019" /> In fact, while "[[Feature phone|dumb phones]]" (or feature phones rather than smartphones) are on the decline around the world, in the U.S., their sales are growing among Generation Z.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mays |first=Liam |date=March 29, 2023 |title=Dumb phones are on the rise in the U.S. as Gen Z looks to limit screen time |work=CNBC |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2023/03/29/dumb-phones-are-on-the-rise-in-the-us-as-gen-z-limits-screen-time.html |access-date=April 12, 2023}}</ref> According to a 2019 YouGov poll, 31% of the U.S. population is willing to pay for music on vinyl, including 26% of Generation Z.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ballard |first=Jamie |date=April 12, 2021 |title=How many Americans are still buying vinyl records? |work=YouGov |url=https://today.yougov.com/topics/media/articles-reports/2019/04/12/record-store-day-2019-records-generations-poll |access-date=November 1, 2021}}</ref> As a matter of fact, Millennials and Generation Z have given life to [[Nostalgia consumption|nostalgia as an industry]] in the late 2010s and early 2020s,<ref name=":29">{{Cite news |last=Fischer |first=Sara |date=October 17, 2021 |title=TikTok drives new nostalgia economy |url=https://www.axios.com/2021/10/17/tiktok-gen-z-nostalgia-millennials-fashion-music-trends |access-date=October 15, 2024 |work=Axios}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Carroll |first=Leah |date=December 18, 2023 |title=Nostalgia marketing is powerful. 'Nowstalgia' might be even more compelling. |url=https://www.bbc.com/worklife/article/20231215-nostalgia-marketing-is-powerful-nowstalgia-might-be-even-more-compelling |access-date=October 15, 2024 |work=BBC Worklife}}</ref> a trend that coincides with the resurgence of some cultural phenomena of the late 1990s and early 2000s ([[Year 2000 problem|Y2K]]), such the television series ''[[Friends]]'' (1994–2004), something that is well-received among young people despite its age.<ref name="YPulse-2020" /> Nostalgia has also contributed to the anticipation and subsequent commercial success of the summer film ''[[Barbie (film)|Barbie]]'' (2023) based on a well-known doll of the same name, even though it was intended for adults rather than children.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lerman |first=Rachel |date=April 21, 2023 |title=Can nostalgia make the Barbie movie a win for Mattel? |newspaper=The Washington Post |department=Business |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2023/04/21/barbie-movie-mattel-adults/ |access-date=December 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230421185938/https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2023/04/21/barbie-movie-mattel-adults/ |archive-date=April 21, 2023}}</ref>

Millennials and Generation Z on average begin using cosmetics in their mid-teens, or a few years earlier than the Baby Boomers and Generation X.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 20, 2026 |title=Why the beauty industry is booming |url=https://www.economist.com/business/2026/01/20/why-the-beauty-industry-is-booming |access-date=March 5, 2026 |work=The Economist}}</ref>

==== Food and drinks ====
[[File:Chick-fil-A Austin-TX.jpg|thumb|300x300px|Chick-fil-A is the most popular fast-food enterprise among American youths.]]According to a 2025 report from the Bank of America, Generation Z consumes less alcohol and prefer different diets than previous cohorts.<ref name=":48" /> Generation Z is more likely than young people in the past to try out new cuisines.
