Here's what being child-free means for your money |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2024/09/24/what-a-sink-dink-or-dinky-lifestyle-means-for-your-money.html |access-date=October 24, 2024 |work=CNBC}}</ref> Many of them are seeking to be sterilization procedures ([[Vasectomy|vasectomies]] for men and [[tubal ligation]] for women),<ref name="Leanne">{{Cite news |last=Leanne |first=Italie |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Gen Z, millennials speak out on reluctance to become parents |url=https://apnews.com/article/covid-health-millennials-fcaa60313baf717312c6e68f12eb53ff |access-date=August 30, 2022 |work=Associated Press}}</ref><ref name=":410">{{Cite news |last=Ungar |first=Laura |date=September 11, 2024 |title=More women had their tubes tied after Roe v. Wade was overturned |url=https://apnews.com/article/abortion-tubal-ligations-tying-tubes-dobbs-roe-jama-2ec56d7f2707db083e513bdc74a5016d |access-date=October 24, 2024 |work=Associated Press}}</ref> an uptick most pronounced in politically conservative states, where abortion, and even contraception and sterilization, could be restricted or banned following the Supreme Court decision ''Dobbs v. Jackson'' (2022).<ref name=":211">{{Cite news |last1=Neal |first1=Jennifer Watling |last2=Watling |first2=Jennifer |date=September 30, 2024 |title=Voters without kids are in the political spotlight – but they're not all the same |url=https://theconversation.com/voters-without-kids-are-in-the-political-spotlight-but-theyre-not-all-the-same-239025 |access-date=October 24, 2024 |work=The Conversation}}</ref><ref name=":410" /> Some have chosen to have pets in lieu of children, and they frequently refer to these animals as members of their families or their own children ("fur babies").<ref name="Twenge-2023a2">{{Cite book |last=Twenge |first=Jean |title=Generations: The Real Differences Between Gen Z, Millennials, Gen X, Boomers, and Silents—and What The Mean for America's Future |publisher=Atria Books |year=2023 |isbn=978-1-9821-8161-1 |location=New York |chapter=Chapter 8: The Future}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Blake |first=Suzanne |date=June 4, 2024 |title=Gen Z Is Choosing Pets Over Children |url=https://www.newsweek.com/gen-z-choosing-pets-over-children-1908186 |access-date=April 27, 2025 |work=Newsweek}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pearcy |first=Aimee |date=November 7, 2024 |title=Generation Fido |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/millennials-raising-pets-instead-kids-spoiled-dogs-cats-anxiety-health-2024-11 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241108044434/https://www.businessinsider.com/millennials-raising-pets-instead-kids-spoiled-dogs-cats-anxiety-health-2024-11 |archive-date=November 8, 2024 |access-date=November 14, 2024 |work=Business Insider}}</ref> Generation Z prefer to prioritize professional life and individual self-discovery, are concerned with financial constraints driven by high inflation and taxes, and dislike the perceived constraints of family life.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-05 |title=Opinion {{!}} Gen Z on Marriage: In This Economy? |url=https://www.wsj.com/opinion/gen-z-on-marriage-in-this-economy-matrimony-young-people-950e9723 |access-date=2026-04-05 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> Those who wish to be parents want to achieve financial security and to be in a serious relationship first.<ref name=":47" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Carter |first=Christine Michel |title=Gen-Z Women Are Preparing For Working Motherhood In Two Very Different Ways |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/christinecarter/2026/02/19/gen-z-women-are-preparing-for-working-motherhood-in-two-very-different-ways/ |access-date=2026-02-26 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> 

=== Sexual orientation and gender identity ===
In February 2021, [[Gallup (company)|Gallup]] reported that 15.9% of American adults born between 1997 and 2002 identified as [[LGBT]]. Of those, 11.5% were [[bisexual]] while 2% said they were [[lesbian]], [[gay]], or [[transgender]]. Overall, a greater share American adults in Generation Z identifies as LGBT than those in previous generational cohorts.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Jones|first1=Jeffrey M.|date=February 24, 2021|title=LGBT Identification Rises to 5.6% in Latest U.S. Estimate|url=https://news.gallup.com/poll/329708/lgbt-identification-rises-latest-estimate.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210224194441/https://news.gallup.com/poll/329708/lgbt-identification-rises-latest-estimate.aspx|archive-date=February 24, 2021|access-date=February 26, 2021|publisher=Gallup|location=Washington, D.C.}}</ref>

[[Public Religion Research Institute|PRRI]] reported that up to 28% of Zoomers in America said they belonged to the [[LGBT|LGBTQ]] community, significantly more than the 16% of Millennials and 7% of previous generations.<ref name="PRRI-LGBTQ">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-22 |title=A Political and Cultural Glimpse Into America's Future: Generation Z's Views on Generational Change and the Challenges and Opportunities Ahead {{!}} PRRI |url=https://www.prri.org/research/generation-zs-views-on-generational-change-and-the-challenges-and-opportunities-ahead-a-political-and-cultural-glimpse-into-americas-future/ |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=PRRI {{!}} At the intersection of religion, values, and public life. |language=en-US}}</ref> Among Zoomer adults in the United States between the ages of 18 and 25, 72% identified as heterosexual, 15% as bisexual, 5% as gay or lesbian, and 8% as "other".<ref name="CNN-LBGTQ">{{Cite web |last=Chavez |first=Nicole |date=2024-01-25 |title=Gen Z adults identify as LGBTQ at much higher rates than older Americans, report shows |url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/01/25/us/gen-z-adults-lgbtq-identity-reaj/index.html |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=CNN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-24 |title=Nearly 30% of Gen Z adults identify as LGBTQ, national survey finds |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/nbc-out/out-news/nearly-30-gen-z-adults-identify-lgbtq-national-survey-finds-rcna135510 |access-date=2024-03-18 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref>

== Use of information and communications technologies (ICT) ==
=== Use of ICT in general ===
<gallery mode="packed" heights="240">

</gallery>Members of Generation Z have acquired a "digital bond to the Internet" from a very young age.<ref name="turner">{{cite journal | last1 = Turner | first1 = Anthony | year = 2015 | title = Generation Z: Technology And Social Interest | url = | journal = Journal of Individual Psychology | volume = 71 | issue = 2| pages = 103–113 | doi=10.1353/jip.2015.0021| s2cid = 146564218 }}</ref> According to the Pew Research Center, a defining feature of this cohort is that the majority owns a cell phone.<ref name="Lenhart-2015" /> About one quarter of teens are almost constantly online<ref name="Lenhart-2015">{{cite web |last=Lenhart |first=Amanda |date=8 April 2015 |title=Teens, Social Media & Technology Overview 2015 |url=http://www.pewinternet.org/2015/04/09/teens-social-media-technology-2015 |access-date=5 December 2015 |website=Pew Research Center |publisher=Pew Research Center Internet Science Tech RSS}}</ref> and 80% feel distressed if separated from their electronic gadgets.<ref name="Desjardins-2019">{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/agenda/2019/02/meet-generation-z-the-newest-member-to-the-workforce/|title=Generation Z: What to expect from the newest addition to the workforce|last=Desjardins|first=Jeff|date=February 19, 2019|website=World Economic Forum|access-date=June 16, 2019}}</ref> Generation Z spends on average six hours each day on the Internet, much of it playing video games.<ref name="Solmon-2019a">{{Cite news|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/how-kids-are-adapting-to-a-cashless-culture|title=How kids are adapting to a cashless culture|last=Solmon|first=Paul|date=March 7, 2019|work=PBS Newshour|access-date=May 17, 2019}}</ref> That much of Generation Z is growing up with constant access to Internet-enabled devices has undermined parental authority and control, prompting concerns over the sort of information children are exposed to while surfing the World Wide Web.<ref name="Pickhardt-2023">{{Cite journal |last=Pickhardt |first=Carl E. |date=August 2023 |title=The Challenging Combination of Childhood Curiosity and Internet Access |url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/intl/articles/202307/kids-online-what-concerns-experts-most |journal=Psychology Today |pages=34–5}}</ref>

=== Digital literacy ===
Despite being commonly known as "digital natives", Generation Z is not necessarily digitally literate. The 2018 [[International Computer and Information Literacy Study]] (ICILS), conducted on 42,000 eighth-graders (or equivalents) from 14 countries, found that only two percent were sufficiently proficient with information devices to justify that description, and only 19% could work independently with computers to gather information and manage their work.<ref name="Strauss-2019">{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/education/2019/11/16/todays-kids-may-be-digital-natives-new-study-shows-they-arent-close-being-computer-literate/?outputType=amp|title=Today's kids might be digital natives — but a new study shows they aren't close to being computer literate|last=Strauss|first=Valerie|date=November 16, 2019|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=November 21, 2019|department=Education}}</ref> In the U.S., 90% reached Level 1, 66% Level 2, 25% Level 3, and 2% Level 4.<ref name="Strauss-2019" /> Among American eighth-graders, 72% said they searched for information on the Internet at least once a week or every school day, and 65% reported they were autodidactic information finders on the Internet.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nces.ed.gov/surveys/icils/icils2018/theme1.asp|title=ICILS 2018 U.S. Results|last=|first=|date=2019|website=National Center for Education Statistics|access-date=November 21, 2019}}</ref>

The role of Generation Z in the future "digital economy" remains uncertain as they still lack the skills they need to join the workforce.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Berger |first=Chloe |date=February 2, 2023 |title=America is failing to prepare Gen Z to enter the workforce due to a 'glaring' gap in tech skills |url=https://fortune.com/2023/02/02/gen-z-tech-skills-gap-workplace/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230202142852/https://fortune.com/2023/02/02/gen-z-tech-skills-gap-workplace/ |archive-date=February 2, 2023 |work=Fortune}}</ref> At least initially, they struggle with office items such as printers or scanners.<ref name=":282"/> Many are also unfamiliar with [[touch typing]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wells |first=Georgia |date=August 24, 2024 |title=Gen Z-ers Are Computer Whizzes. Just Don't Ask Them to Type. |url=https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/gen-z-typing-computers-keyboards-c83d15f0 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250129185130/https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/gen-z-typing-computers-keyboards-c83d15f0 |archive-date=January 29, 2025 |access-date=March 8, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref>

=== Use of social media networks ===
Almost all Americans who were in their teens and 20s during the late 2010s and early 2020s are on at least one social-media platform.<ref name=":21">{{Cite news |last1=Hadero |first1=Haleluya |last2=Ortutay |first2=Barbara |date=October 8, 2024 |title=TikTok is designed to be addictive to kids and causes them harm, US states' lawsuits say |url=https://apnews.com/article/tiktok-lawsuit-youth-mental-health-2993f8e70d2e3d4eab9988df168fb948 |access-date=October 13, 2024 |work=Associated Press}}</ref> [[YouTube]] was the most popular in 2024, followed by TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat. Meanwhile, Facebook and Twitter have lost grounds among teenagers compared to the 2010s.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Faverio |first1=Michelle |last2=Sidoti |first2=Olivia |date=December 12, 2024 |title=Teens, Social Media and Technology 2024 |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/2024/12/12/teens-social-media-and-technology-2024/ |access-date=May 19, 2025 |website=Pew Research Center}}</ref> About three quarters checked their accounts multiple times a day.<ref name=":32">{{Cite journal |last1=Young |first1=Emily |last2=McCain |first2=Jessica L. |display-authors=1 |date=October 10, 2024 |title=Frequent Social Media Use and Experiences with Bullying Victimization, Persistent Feelings of Sadness or Hopelessness, and Suicide Risk Among High School Students — Youth Risk Behavior Survey, United States, 2023 |journal=Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report Supplements |publisher=Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) |volume=73 |issue=4 |pages=23–30 |doi=10.15585/mmwr.su7304a3|doi-access=free |pmid=39378186 |pmc=11559676 }}</ref> Members of Generation Z are more likely to "follow" others on social media than "share" and use different types of social media for different purposes.<ref name="Seemiller-2016a">{{Cite book|title=Generation Z Goes to College|last=Seemiller|first=Corey|publisher=Jossey-Bass|year=2016|isbn=978-1-119-14345-1|location=|pages=}}</ref> Very few expressed concern about third parties being able to access their data as they share more personal information more often compared to previous generations. Most have uploaded photographs of themselves, stated their interests, given their school names, posted their locations, and revealed their relationship statuses.<ref name="Madden">{{cite news |last=Madden |first=Mary |display-authors=etal |date=21 May 2013 |title=Teens, Social Media, and Privacy. |work=Pew Research Center |url=http://www.pewinternet.org/2013/05/21/teens-social-media-and-privacy/ |access-date=10 December 2015}}</ref> As a cohort, Generation Z finds validation and social support on social media,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Riegel |first=Sophie |date=January–February 2025 |title=Winging It |url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/us/articles/202501/what-it-means-to-be-an-adult-today |journal=Psychology Today |pages=29–30}}</ref> where they develop their own [[Personal identity|individual identities]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Marano |first=Hara Estroff |date=September–October 2023 |title=Owning Yourself in A Socially Mediated Age |journal=Psychology Today |pages=32–33}}</ref> On the other hand, only a minority engaged in political conversations on social media networks.<ref name="Business Wire-2019" /> Despite their heavy usage of social media, a majority believe that life was better before the emergence of these platforms.<ref name=":29" />
[[File:Banning_of_TikTok_on_state_devices_in_the_United_States.svg|thumb|400x400px|Map current as of March 2024. As of April 2024, more than 30 states have [[Restrictions on TikTok in the United States|banned the use of TikTok]] on government devices, including some university computer Wifi networks, though students can still use their own devices and data plans.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Maheshwari |first1=Sapna |last2=Holpuch |first2=Amanda |date=April 26, 2024 |title=Why the U.S. Is Forcing TikTok to Be Sold or Banned |url=https://www.nytimes.com/article/tiktok-ban.html |access-date=June 30, 2024 |work=The New York Times |quote=More than 30 states, and New York City, have joined the federal government in banning TikTok on government-issued devices. Many colleges have blocked it from campus Wi-Fi networks. But students often just switch to cellular data to use the app.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Gleeson |first1=Cailey |title=These 39 States Already Ban TikTok From Government Devices |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/caileygleeson/2024/03/12/these-39-states-already-ban-tiktok-from-government-devices/ |website=[[Forbes]] |access-date=5 January 2025 |date=12 March 2024}}</ref>{{legend|#AC2522;|Ban enacted}} {{legend|#DEDEDE;|No ban}}]]
While teens may dislike certain aspects of [[Facebook]], such as excessive sharing, they continue to use it because participation is important in terms of socializing with peers.<ref name="Madden" /> Teens typically keep their Facebook accounts private and make their [[Twitter]] accounts public, partly because of the number of adults on the former.<ref name="Madden" /> Speed and reliability are important factors in choice of social networking platform. This need for quick communication is apparent in the popularity of apps like [[Vine (service)|Vine]]<ref group="note">This service is no longer operational.</ref> or [[Snapchat]] and the prevalent use of [[emojis]].<ref name="Williams">{{cite news |last=Williams |first=Alex |date=18 September 2015 |title=Move Over, Millennials, Here Comes Generation Z |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/20/fashion/move-over-millennials-here-comes-generation-z.html |access-date=16 December 2015 |newspaper=New York Times}}</ref> By the early 2020s, [[TikTok]] has become one of the most popular social networks among teenagers and young adults,<ref name="Barinka-2023" /> who frequently use it as a news source<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Leppert |first1=Rebecca |last2=Matsa |first2=Katerina Eva |date=September 17, 2024 |title=More Americans – especially young adults – are regularly getting news on TikTok |url=https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/09/17/more-americans-regularly-get-news-on-tiktok-especially-young-adults/ |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=Pew Research Center}}</ref> and a [[search engine]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Huang |first=Kalley |date=September 16, 2022 |title=For Gen Z, TikTok Is the New Search Engine |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/16/technology/gen-z-tiktok-search-engine.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240511073012/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/09/16/technology/gen-z-tiktok-search-engine.html |archive-date=May 11, 2024 |access-date=October 13, 2024 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> Young Americans are willing to ignore their own government's concerns over issues of user privacy and national security, as well as a possible nationwide [[Restrictions on TikTok in the United States|ban]].<ref name="Sherman-2023">{{Cite news |last=Sherman |first=Natalie |date=March 12, 2023 |title=TikTok users shrug at China fears: 'It's hard to care' |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-64827885 |access-date=March 13, 2023}}</ref>

A notable number of people from Generation Z are the subject of their parents' social media posts. As they grow older, they have opinions about pictures or videos of them being posted online. While some parents do ask for their children's permission before posting, at least some of the time, others simply disregard what their children think.<ref name="Gibson-2019" /> A 2010 report by cybersecurity firm [[AVG Technologies|AVG]] stated that an absolute majority of American children under the age of two had a digital footprint and one in three had their information and photographs posted online within weeks after they were born.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/lifestyles/sc-babies-digital-real-estate-family-1027-20151020-story.html|title=Do newborns need their own websites, email, social media accounts?|last=Bowen|first=Allison|date=October 20, 2015|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=September 7, 2019}}</ref> One of the reasons why children want greater control over their image online is because a college admissions officer or a prospective recruiter might look them up online.<ref name="Gibson-2019">{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/on-parenting/gen-z-kids-are-the-stars-of-their-parents-social-media--and-they-have-opinions-about-that/2019/06/02/c94fc5d4-8180-11e9-95a9-e2c830afe24f_story.html|title=Gen Z kids are the stars of their parents' social media — and they have opinions about that|last=Gibson|first=Caitlin|date=June 3, 2019|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=June 7, 2019}}</ref> As a result, members of Generation Z are careful to make themselves presentable to potential employers on social media. Not only do they take advantage of the various tools that allow them to control who sees what and are more cautious about what they post, they also try to cultivate a "personal brand" online.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2019/04/13/702555175/under-employers-gaze-gen-z-is-biting-its-tongue-on-social-media|title=Under Employers' Gaze, Gen Z Is Biting Its Tongue On Social Media|date=April 13, 2019|website=NPR|access-date=May 12, 2019}}</ref> According to the Pew Research Center, a majority refrain from posting something if they think it might "reflect badly on them in the future."<ref name="Edwards-2015" /> It is quite common for young people to have an alternate Instagram account, "finstas" (fake Instagram accounts).<ref name="Piore-2019" />

There are growing concerns and evidence on the negative impact of social media networks on youth mental health,<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":32" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Kerr |first=Dana |date=January 9, 2024 |title=Under growing pressure, Meta vows to make it harder for teens to see harmful content |url=https://www.npr.org/2024/01/09/1223583540/meta-harmful-content-instagram-harder-teens-facebook |access-date=January 23, 2023 |work=NPR}}</ref><ref name="The Data Team-2018">{{Cite news |last=The Data Team |date=May 18, 2018 |title=How heavy use of social media is linked to mental illness |url=https://www.economist.com/graphic-detail/2018/05/18/how-heavy-use-of-social-media-is-linked-to-mental-illness |access-date=September 5, 2019 |newspaper=The Economist |department=Daily Chart}}</ref><ref>Also see the [[#Health issues|health issues]] of Generation Z.</ref> because these platforms can be addictive;<ref name=":21" /><ref name=":20" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sherman |first=Natalie |date=October 8, 2024 |title=TikTok sued for 'wreaking havoc' on teen mental health |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c20m4k56relo |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=BBC News}}</ref>  and can expose them to inappropriate contents,<ref name="Pickhardt-2023" /><ref name=":31" />  [[cyberbullying]], [[slut-shaming]], and [[body shaming]].<ref name=":31" /><ref name=":32" /><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Frenkel |first1=Sheera |title=An Ugly Truth: Inside Facebook's Battle for Domination |last2=Kang |first2=Cecilia |publisher=Harper |year=2021 |isbn=978-0-06-296067-2 |location=New York |pages=88–89 |chapter=Chapter 4: The Rat Catcher}}</ref> Youth who spend more time on social media tend to have worse body-image issues,<ref name="Goldfield-2023" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Seidman |first1=Gwendolyn |last2=Feigenson |first2=Keith |date=August 2023 |title=The Radical Threat of Photo Filters |url=https://www.psychologytoday.com/intl/blog/close-encounters/202303/will-new-hyper-realistic-video-filters-harm-mental-health |journal=Psychology Today}}</ref> a problem especially serious among
